text: DATAMAKER TRAINING CENTER
Vibe Coding: Build Websites by Describing Them
A hands-on workshop, with no IT background required. Learn to write great prompts, then build a portfolio, an expense tracker and a photo album with AI.
notes: Welcome everyone. By the end of this session every one of you will have built three real projects — without writing code by hand. You type what you want in plain English; the AI builds it.

text: PART 1 · GETTING STARTED
What Is Vibe Coding? In Plain English
Building websites without years of study.
You describe what you want in everyday English. The AI writes the code.  You are the thinker; the AI is the builder.

REAL-LIFE STORY  ·  Teaching a new apprentice
Imagine hiring a skilled apprentice who knows every building technique. You don't teach them HOW to lay bricks; you tell them WHAT you want: “A three-bedroom house with a blue door.” They work out the steps. That is Vibe Coding.

The old way
Study for years before building anything. One typo and everything crashes.

The Vibe Coding way
Describe your idea in English. The AI writes the code. You test it and improve it.

What you need
An internet connection, a free account, and the ability to describe what you want.
THINK ABOUT IT   Have you ever told someone exactly what you wanted, and they did it for you? That is Vibe Coding.
notes: Read the definition aloud, then tell the apprentice story. Ask the think-about-it question and take two or three answers before moving on.

text: PART 1 · GETTING STARTED
Why It Matters
What vibe coding can do for you.

It's for everyone
You don't need to be good at maths or have a computer science background. You just need to describe an idea clearly.

It can grow your income
Businesses, churches and schools need websites. Once you can build one, you can offer it as a service.

It's fast
Things that used to take months of study, you'll start doing today, because the AI does the typing.

You'll build 3 things today
Not theory. A portfolio, an expense tracker and a photo album, all working in your browser.
notes: Go through each card. If you have a personal story about technology changing your life or work, tell it here.

text: PART 1 · GETTING STARTED
Ground Rules for Working With AI
Six rules that will save you a lot of trouble.

You are the boss
The AI is a helper. You decide what is good enough.

Test everything
Always open it in the browser. Never trust code you haven't seen working.

Never share secrets
No passwords, ID numbers, bank details or other people's private information in prompts.

One change at a time
Small requests mean fewer mistakes and easier fixes.

Save every working version
mypage-v1.html, mypage-v2.html… so you can always go back.

Two tries, then ask
If the AI fails twice, raise your hand. A classmate or trainer will help.
notes: Spend extra time on 'Never share secrets': never paste real passwords or other people's personal details into an AI tool.

text: PART 2  ·  WRITING GREAT PROMPTS
What a prompt is  ·  The CLEAR rule  ·  Good vs bad prompts
notes: Part 2 teaches the single most important skill: describing clearly what you want.

text: PART 2 · WRITING GREAT PROMPTS
What Is a Prompt? The Most Important Skill
A prompt is the message you type to the AI. The better your prompt, the better your result.

REAL-LIFE STORY  ·  Ordering at a restaurant
“Give me food” confuses the waiter. “Jollof rice with chicken, extra spicy, no onions please” gets you exactly what you want. The AI is that waiter: the clearer your order, the better your result.
THE CLEAR RULE FOR WRITING PROMPTS
C

Context
What is the project? Who is it for?
L

Language
HTML? CSS? JavaScript? One file?
E

Elements
Which sections and features?
A

Appearance
Colours, style, mood?
R

Result
What should the finished thing do?
notes: Tell the restaurant story, then introduce CLEAR one letter at a time. Ask trainees to write C-L-E-A-R in their notebook.

text: PART 2 · WRITING GREAT PROMPTS
CLEAR in Action: Step by Step
Watch a prompt come together, one letter at a time.
C
I run a small hair salon called Ama's Styles.
L
Use HTML and CSS in one single file.
E
Include a heading, a list of services with prices, opening hours and a phone number.
A
Use purple and white. Friendly and modern, with big easy-to-read text.
R
It must look good on a phone so customers can check prices quickly.
THE FINISHED PROMPT

I run a small hair salon called Ama's Styles. Create a one-page website using HTML and CSS in one single file.
Include a heading, a list of services with prices, our opening hours and a phone number.
Use purple and white. Make it friendly and modern, with big easy-to-read text.
It must look good on a phone so customers can check prices quickly.
notes: Build the prompt with the class: ask for each letter in turn, then join the pieces. Run it live in Claude and open the result.

text: PART 2 · WRITING GREAT PROMPTS
Bad Prompt vs Good Prompt
Same AI, two prompts, very different results.
Bad prompt

“Make me a website.”
Why it fails: the AI doesn't know what KIND of website, what goes in it, or how it should look. You get something random.
Good prompt

“Create a portfolio webpage for me using HTML and CSS. Include a header with my name ‘Ama’, an About Me section, and a Contact section with my email. Use navy and white colours.”
Why it works: the AI knows exactly what to build.
The rule:  if your prompt could get 10 different answers, it needs more detail.
YOUR TURN   Turn “Make me a website” into a CLEAR prompt for something you care about: a church, a shop, a football club. Write it on paper. Then compare with your neighbour: who gave more detail?
notes: Run both prompts live and compare the results. Then give trainees 3–4 minutes for the 'your turn' exercise on paper.

text: PART 3  ·  YOUR PORTFOLIO WEBSITE
How a webpage works  ·  Build it  ·  Copy, save, open  ·  Style it
notes: Part 3 is the first build: every trainee creates their own portfolio website and opens it in the browser.

text: PART 3 · PROJECT 1: PORTFOLIO
A Webpage Is Like a House
You won't write these yourself, but knowing who does what helps you ask for the right change.

HTML
The walls and rooms
The structure: headings, paragraphs, pictures, buttons. What is ON the page.

CSS
The paint and decoration
The look: colours, sizes, spacing, layout. How the page LOOKS.

JavaScript
The electricity
The action: clicks, calculations, saving. What the page DOES.
WHICH PART DO I ASK THE AI TO CHANGE?
notes: Use the house analogy, then quiz the class with the table: read each sentence and ask which part is responsible.

text: PART 3 · PROJECT 1: PORTFOLIO
What Is the Portfolio?
Project 1: a personal website that tells the world who you are.

REAL-LIFE STORY  ·  A business card that never runs out
At an event you hand someone a business card. A portfolio is that card on the internet: it shows who you are, what you can do and how to reach you, and it works 24 hours a day.
SECTIONS YOU WILL BUILD

Header & menu
Your name and links to each section

About me
Three sentences about you

Skills
Four skill cards

Projects
Your work, like the apps you build today

Contact
A public email address
notes: Explain the portfolio as an online business card. Point out the Projects section: later today they can list their expense tracker and photo album there.

text: PART 3 · PROJECT 1: PORTFOLIO
Build It: Your Portfolio
Fill in the [brackets] on paper first. Then type it into Claude.
YOUR PROMPT

Create a personal portfolio website in one single HTML file, with the CSS inside the same file. My name is [YOUR NAME] and I am learning to build websites.
Include these sections, in order:
1. A header with my name and a menu linking to each section
2. About Me: [3 FACTS ABOUT YOU]
3. Skills: 4 cards with [SKILL 1], [SKILL 2], [SKILL 3], [SKILL 4]
4. Projects: 3 cards, each with a title, a short description and a View button
5. Contact: my email [PUBLIC EMAIL]
6. A footer that says “Built with Vibe Coding”
Use [YOUR FAVOURITE COLOURS]. Make it modern and friendly, and make it look good on a phone. Give me the complete code to copy.
Check your prompt

C: a portfolio for you
L: one HTML file
E: the 6 sections
A: your colours
R: works on a phone
SAFETY   Use a public email only. No phone numbers or home address.
notes: Give trainees time to fill in the brackets on paper. Check a few prompts against CLEAR before they type them. Then everyone sends their prompt to Claude.

text: PART 3 · PROJECT 1: PORTFOLIO
Copy, Save, Open
Follow these four steps for every project: portfolio.html, expenses.html, album.html.

Read it first
Before copying, read what the AI wrote. Does it match what you asked for?

Copy the code
Click the Copy button on the code box (top-right corner), or select all the code and press Ctrl+C.

Paste & save
Paste into Notepad (Ctrl+V). File → Save As → type: All Files, encoding: UTF-8 → name it portfolio.html in your vibe-coding folder.

Open it!
Double-click portfolio.html. It opens in your browser. That's your website!
WATCH OUT   Saved it as portfolio.html.txt by mistake? Save again and choose “All Files” in the Save as type box. When your page opens, celebrate. You just built a website!
notes: Demonstrate all four steps slowly on the projector. The most common problem is saving as portfolio.html.txt — show the 'All Files' option clearly.

text: PART 3 · PROJECT 1: PORTFOLIO
Style Your Portfolio
Describe the look in plain English. The AI writes all the CSS. Stay in the same chat.
PROMPT: STYLE MY PORTFOLIO

Improve the styling of my portfolio. Keep everything in the same single HTML file.
- Header: dark navy background (#1A2B5F), white text, centred, big and bold
- Menu: links side by side, white, no underline, turn teal when I hover over them
- Every section: plenty of space above and below (80 pixels)
- Skill cards: light blue background, rounded corners, a soft shadow
- Project cards: white background, thin grey border, rounded corners, a shadow
- Footer: dark grey background, white text, centred
Make it clean and modern, professional but friendly. Give me the complete updated code.
TRY THIS   Pick your own colours and style. The skill is describing a look in words, not copying this one.
notes: Run this prompt live, then let trainees write their own version with their own colours. They paste the new code over the old in Notepad, save, and refresh the browser.

text: PART 4  ·  MAKE IT BETTER
Refine  ·  Speak human  ·  Fix problems  ·  Level up
notes: Part 4 turns a first draft into something trainees are proud of, and teaches them how to fix problems on their own.

text: PART 4 · MAKE IT BETTER
The Refine Loop
Nobody gets it perfect first time. Good builders go round this loop many times.
Ask
Test
Describe
Save
Send one clear request
Open it in the browser
Say what you SEE is wrong
Keep each working version
Rules for a good refine

One change per message
Say WHERE on the page: “the heading”, “the second card”
Describe what you see, not what you think the code is
Paste the new code over the old, save, then refresh the browser (F5)
If it gets worse, go back to your last saved version
notes: Draw this loop on the board. The most common beginner mistake is asking for five changes at once, then not knowing which one broke the page. Show how to paste the new code, save and press F5.

text: PART 4 · MAKE IT BETTER
Speak Human, Not Tech
Describe problems in everyday words; the AI understands them perfectly.
PRACTICE   In pairs: one is the client and says “I don't like this.” The designer asks: “What exactly don't you like?” Be specific!
notes: The left column is what experienced coders say; the right column is all trainees need. Do the pair practice for two minutes.

text: PART 4 · MAKE IT BETTER
Level Up: Try These Challenges
Pick one, send it, test it. Finished? Try the next one.
CHALLENGE 1: A BUTTON THAT DOES SOMETHING
Add a button under my heading that says “Change colour”. When I click it, the page background changes to a random soft colour.
CHALLENGE 2: MAKE IT MOVE
When I hover over a skill card, make it lift up gently with a bigger shadow. When the page loads, fade everything in smoothly.
CHALLENGE 3: MAKE IT SMART
Show a greeting under my name that changes with the time of day: “Good morning”, “Good afternoon” or “Good evening”.
notes: These three challenges add JavaScript and animation. Fast trainees can do all three; everyone should try at least one. Remind them: save a copy of the working portfolio before each challenge.

text: PART 4 · MAKE IT BETTER
When the AI Gets It Wrong: What to Do
Wrong answers happen to everyone. Here's how to fix them.
Ask yourself:  “What information was missing from my prompt?” Then add it and try again.
notes: When a trainee hits a problem, ask the room what was missing from the prompt instead of fixing it for them.

text: PART 5  ·  THE EXPENSE TRACKER
Forms  ·  Lists  ·  Totals  ·  Saving  ·  Charts
notes: The first real app: it doesn't just show information, it does things — adds, deletes, calculates and remembers.

text: PART 5 · PROJECT 2: EXPENSE TRACKER
What Is the Expense Tracker App?
Project 2: your first app that DOES things, not just shows things.

REAL-LIFE STORY  ·  A paper budget book, but better
Many families keep a book of money in and money out. The Expense Tracker is that same book on a computer: it adds up by itself, sorts by category, saves by itself, and opens any time.

Add entries
A form: name, amount and category (Food, Transport, Bills…)

Delete entries
Remove any entry with one click

Running total
Updates automatically on every add or delete

Category filter
Press ‘Food’ to see only food spending

Spending chart
A picture of where the money goes

Auto-save
Still there after closing the browser
notes: Ask: who keeps track of their spending? How? Then show the six features. The first prompt builds add, delete and total; the next prompts add filters, saving and a chart.

text: PART 5 · PROJECT 2: EXPENSE TRACKER
Build the Expense Tracker
Start a NEW chat for this project. Save the code as expenses.html.
PROMPT 1: THE FULL APP

Build me a complete expense tracker app in one single HTML file (put the CSS and JavaScript inside the same file).
It should have a form where I type the expense name and the amount, and pick a category: Food, Transport, Bills, Entertainment, Other.
When I click Add, the expense appears in a list below. Each entry shows the name, amount and a red Delete button.
At the bottom, show the total of all amounts, updated automatically. Show amounts in [YOUR CURRENCY, e.g. GH₵].
Make it clean and modern with a teal and white colour scheme.
Test it like this

Add 3 expenses
Is the total correct? Check with a calculator
Delete one: does the total go down?
Click Add with an empty form: what happens?
Refresh the page: where did everything go?
notes: Run the prompt live. The test list teaches trainees to check an app like a user would. The refresh test shows the data disappearing, which sets up the saving prompt on the next slide.

text: PART 5 · PROJECT 2: EXPENSE TRACKER
Make It Smarter: Filters, Saving, Chart
One prompt at a time. Test after each one.
PROMPT 2: CATEGORY FILTER
Add filter buttons above the list: All, Food, Transport, Bills, Entertainment, Other. Clicking one shows only that category and its total. Highlight the active button.
PROMPT 3: SAVE THE DATA
Save all expenses with localStorage whenever I add or delete one. When I open or refresh the page, show the saved expenses. If there are none, start empty.
PROMPT 4: SPENDING CHART
Add a doughnut chart above the list showing how much I spent in each category. Use Chart.js. Update it every time I add or delete an expense.
notes: localStorage is like a notepad next to your computer: close the browser, come back tomorrow, and your notes are still there. Show it: add expenses, refresh, still there. Note that it saves only on that one device and browser. The chart needs an internet connection because Chart.js loads from the web.

text: PART 6  ·  THE PHOTO ALBUM
Gallery  ·  Lightbox  ·  Upload  ·  Search  ·  Animations
notes: A visual, satisfying project. Trainees build one feature at a time and finish with animations that make it feel professional.

text: PART 6 · PROJECT 3: PHOTO ALBUM
What Is the Photo Album App?
Project 3: a gallery you build yourself.

REAL-LIFE STORY  ·  A digital photo album
Remember photo albums with plastic sleeves, passed around at family gatherings? This is that, on the internet. Upload photos, add captions, sort them into albums, search, and click any photo to see it big.

Upload photos
Choose images from your phone or computer

Photo grid
A neat grid that fits every screen size

Captions
A short description under each photo

Albums
Named groups: Family, Work, Travel

Search
Type a word to find matching captions

Lightbox
Click a photo to see it big, full-screen
notes: Show the six features. Rule for this project: one feature at a time — never ask for everything at once.

text: PART 6 · PROJECT 3: PHOTO ALBUM
Build the Gallery and the Lightbox
New chat, new file: album.html. One feature at a time.
PROMPT 1: THE GALLERY GRID

Create a photo gallery web app in one HTML file. Show photos in a grid of 3 columns. Use placeholder photos from picsum.photos/300/200 for now. Each photo card shows the image, a caption below and a small album badge. Make the grid responsive: 2 columns on tablets, 1 column on phones.
PROMPT 2: LIGHTBOX, CLICK TO ENLARGE

Add a lightbox. When I click any photo, it opens big and centred on a dark background, with the caption below in white text. A large × button at the top right closes it, and clicking the dark background also closes it. Also let me close it with the Escape key.
notes: Run prompt 1 and check the grid. Then run prompt 2. Placeholder photos load from the internet, so trainees need to be online.

text: PART 6 · PROJECT 3: PHOTO ALBUM
Upload, Search and Animations
Uploaded photos may vanish on refresh; browser storage is small. That's fine for practice.
PROMPT 3: UPLOAD REAL PHOTOS
Add a photo upload button. When I choose images from my computer or phone, they appear in the grid. Let me type a caption for each, and choose several photos at once.
PROMPT 4: SEARCH AND ALBUMS
Add a search box: as I type, show only photos whose caption contains those words. Add album buttons (All, Family, Work, Travel) and let me pick an album when I upload.
PROMPT 5: ANIMATIONS
Hovering a photo card lifts it gently with a bigger shadow. On page load, cards fade in one after another. The lightbox fades in smoothly. Use CSS only.
notes: Remind trainees to use photos they are happy to share — not other people's private pictures. Browser storage holds only about 5 MB, so uploaded photos may not survive a refresh; real apps store photos on a server. Animations: like a shop window display — they make the app feel professional, but too many become distracting.

text: PART 7  ·Your Own App: Your Idea, Your Build
Gallery  ·  Lightbox  ·  Upload  ·  Search  ·  Animations
notes: A visual, satisfying project. Trainees build one feature at a time and finish with animations that make it feel professional.

text: The Own Project: Freedom and Responsibility
Everything you have learned comes together in something YOU choose to build.

The goal
Build a real, live, useful web app, something that solves a real problem or that you genuinely want to exist, using everything from this course.
THE 5-DAY PLAN

DAY
16

Idea & plan
Pick the idea. Write the plan. No code yet.

DAY
17

Build the MVP
Only the must-have features.

DAY
18

Add features
Should-haves, one at a time.

DAY
19

Polish & publish
Quality checklist, then go live.

DAY
20

Showcase
Present to the class.
notes: Explain the freedom — and the responsibility. They choose the idea, but they must finish and publish it in five days. Show the 5-day plan and stress Day 16: planning only, no code. Trainees who skip planning usually run out of time.

text: Finding Your Idea
Three questions to unlock your idea. Think local.

What do you do with paper or a notebook that could be done better on a computer?
Keeping a list, writing notes, tracking something, planning events.

What website or app do you wish existed for YOUR community, business or family?
Prayer schedules, market price lists, school timetables, community announcements.

Who do you know who has a problem a simple webpage could solve?
A trader who needs a catalogue, a church events page, a school resources page.
▶  BRAINSTORMING PROMPT

I want to build a web app as my final project. I am interested in [YOUR INTEREST]. The problem I want to solve is [DESCRIBE A PROBLEM]. My users are [WHO WILL USE IT]. I have 4 days to build it. Suggest 5 simple ideas I could realistically build. For each: a name, what it does, and the 3 must-have features.
notes: Give trainees five minutes to answer the three questions on paper before they touch the computer. Then they use the brainstorming prompt. Encourage local, practical ideas — they are easier to explain at the showcase and more useful afterwards.

text: Plan Small: The MVP
MVP = Minimum Viable Product: the smallest version that actually does the job.

REAL-LIFE STORY  ·  A skateboard before a car
Someone needs to get from A to B. A car would be better, but takes too long to build. A skateboard gets them moving today. Build the skateboard FIRST, then add to it. Your MVP is the skateboard.
EXAMPLE: A CHURCH EVENTS PAGE

Must have
Without it, the app is useless
A list of events with date, time and place

Should have
Important, but can wait a day
Filter events by month

Nice to have
Only if there's time left
An “Add to my calendar” button
notes: Tell the skateboard story. Then walk through the church example and ask trainees to sort their own features into the three columns. Rule: Day 17 builds only the must-haves. If a must-have list has more than three items, it's too big.

text: The Planning Prompt: Before Any Code
Don't jump straight into building. Plan first: it saves time.
▶  PLANNING PROMPT

I want to build a web app called [NAME]. It will [ONE-SENTENCE DESCRIPTION]. The people who will use it are [WHO].
Before we write any code, please:
1. List the 3 must-have features
2. List 2 nice-to-have features
3. Suggest what to build on Day 1, Day 2, Day 3 and Day 4
4. Tell me if anything I'm imagining is too complex for 4 days
Be honest about what is realistic.
Check your plan

Can it be built in 4 days?
3 or fewer must-haves?
No private data collected?
Can you explain it in one sentence?
Show your plan to your trainer before Day 17
notes: Every trainee runs the planning prompt and writes the plan in their notebook. Then they bring the plan to you for sign-off before any code. Check the four questions on the right. Pay attention to private data: an app that collects names and phone numbers needs much more care — steer them away from that for this project.

text: When the AI Gets It Wrong: What to Do
Wrong answers happen to everyone. Here is what to do.
Ask yourself:  “What information was missing from my prompt?” Then add it and try again.
notes: Use this any day — it fits especially well on Days 17 and 18, when trainees work on their own. When a trainee hits a problem, don't fix it for them: ask the class what was missing from the prompt. The last row is a lifesaver: a long, messy chat often confuses the AI, and a fresh start fixes it.

text: WRAP-UP
Show & Tell
Swap seats, look at each other's projects, and share what you built.

Swap laptops
Can your neighbour use your apps without you explaining them?

Two stars
Tell them two things you really like about their projects.

One wish
Suggest one change, and the prompt they could use to make it.

Want a link you can share on WhatsApp?
Your projects are only on your laptop right now. To put it online for free, open Lovable, paste in your prompt and press Publish, or ask your trainer about GitHub + Vercel.
notes: Give pairs five minutes. Then invite two or three trainees to show their page on the projector. Mention the publishing options for those who want a shareable link after the session.

text: You built 3 projects today. Keep going!

Practise
30 minutes a day. Rebuild a project with a new idea.

Your own idea
Use CLEAR to build an app you wish existed.

Build for someone
A simple page for a local shop, church or school.

Teach a friend
Explaining CLEAR to someone else makes you better at it.
Questions?
notes: Congratulate the class — everyone built a portfolio, an expense tracker and a photo album today. Share next steps and take questions.
Thank you.
